title: Never Go With Your Gut: How Pioneering Leaders Make the Best Decisions and Avoid Business Disasters
author: Gleb Tsipursky
target_audience: Anyone interested in behavioral science and cognitive bias
core_themes: The dangers of relying on intuition in business decisions
How cognitive biases lead to flawed judgment
The value of evidence-based, analytical thinking
Strategies to foster critical thinking in organizations
primary_purpose: To expose the fallacies and risks of gut-based decision making in business, and to equip leaders with practical, science-driven strategies and tools to improve judgment, minimize costly errors, and build thriving organizations.

structure_format.organization: Organized into thematic chapters, each focusing on specific cognitive biases and their implications, followed by actionable guidance and case studies
features: Real-world case studies of business failures and successes

key_concepts_lessons: Human intuition is often unreliable, especially in complex or high-stakes business environments.
Cognitive biases—such as confirmation bias, overconfidence, and the optimism bias—contribute to poor decision-making.
Leaders can train themselves and their teams to identify and counteract these biases.
A structured, reflective approach anchored in behavioral science leads to consistently better outcomes.
Adopting evidence-based decision frameworks can help organizations avoid preventable disasters and maximize success.
Cultural change toward analytical thinking must be intentional and sustained.
notable_features: Integration of cutting-edge behavioral science with business practice
Focus on actionable tools and checklists for leaders
Illustrative stories from major companies and organizations
Self-assessment tools to diagnose personal and organizational decision weaknesses
cultural_historical_context: Published in a time when both corporate scandals and the ‘move fast and break things’ Silicon Valley culture exposed the risks of impulse-driven decisions, the book addresses the need for rigor and science in modern business leadership.
reception_impact: Appreciated for bringing behavioral science into mainstream business advice
Praised for its practical, no-nonsense approach to decision-making improvement
Recommended by leadership coaches and organizational consultants
Some readers note repetition in coverage of biases, but value the actionable content
comparable_titles: Thinking, Fast and Slow by Daniel Kahneman
Decisive: How to Make Better Choices in Life and Work by Chip Heath and Dan Heath
The Art of Thinking Clearly by Rolf Dobelli
